info.title: Unified Approvals API
info.description:
The Unified Approvals Connector is the HTTP API for managing approvals on Workfront document versions. Use it to create approvals, build multi-stage workflows with conditional stage triggers, add and remind participants, record decisions, manage reusable approval templates, search across every approval the requesting user can see, and retrieve AI brand-review results captured by bot reviewers on a stage.

## Authentication

This API is for Adobe IMS **technical accounts** (OAuth Server-to-Server credentials from the Adobe Developer Console). Send the technical account's access token as a Bearer token:

| Header | Value |
|--------|-------|
| `Authorization` | `Bearer <access token>` |
| `x-api-key` | The `client_id` of the technical account |
| `wf-userid` | The Workfront user the request acts as |

Only the endpoints documented here are available to technical accounts. A request to any other path is rejected with `401`. A token that does not belong to a technical account, for example a user's token, is also rejected with `401`.

> **Authentication errors**
>
> | Condition | HTTP status | Body |
> |-----------|-------------|------|
> | Token invalid or expired, not a technical account's, or the endpoint is not available to technical accounts | 401 | `{"message": "Unauthorized", "statusCode": 401}` |
> | A required header such as `wf-userid` or `wf-lane` is missing | 400 | `message` names the missing header |
> | `Authorization` header absent | 403 | `error_code` `403010`, returned by the Adobe I/O gateway |
> | `x-api-key` header absent | 403 | `error_code` `403000`, returned by the Adobe I/O gateway |
>
> The gateway checks for missing credentials before the request reaches the service. The service itself returns the `401` and `400` responses above and does not add an `error_code`.

## Errors

Every error response has `message` and `statusCode`. Errors that come from a business rule also carry a stable `code` in `response.code`; branch on that rather than on `message`. A `503` includes a `Retry-After` header: wait that many seconds, then retry.

## Asset Types

Endpoints currently only support `DOCV` (Workfront document version) as the `assetType` path parameter.


## Base URL

`https://workfront.adobe.io/workfront-approvals/`

## Endpoint Groups

| Tag | Base path |
|-----|-----------|
| Approvals | `/api/v1/approvals` |
| Grouped Approvals | `/api/v1/grouped-approvals` |
| Templates | `/api/v1/templates` |
| Bots | `/api/v1/bots` |
| Bot Reviews | `/api/v1/bot-reviews` |
| Search | `/api/v1/search` |

All endpoints use the authentication described above.

Bearer.description: Access token of an Adobe IMS technical account (OAuth Server-to-Server), from the Adobe Developer Console. Tokens for other kinds of accounts are rejected with `401`.

StageId.name: stageId
StageId.description: The ID of the approval stage

TemplateId.name: templateId
TemplateId.description: The ID of the approval template

XRequestId.name: x-request-id
XRequestId.description: Unique identifier for request tracing. Auto-generated if not provided. Any string is accepted; it is returned in the `x-request-id` response header.

XCorrelationId.name: x-correlation-id
XCorrelationId.description: Unique identifier for correlation across multiple service calls. Auto-generated if not provided.

XApiKey.name: x-api-key
XApiKey.description: `client_id` of the Adobe Developer Console technical account. Identifies the calling integration to the AIO gateway.

XGwSubdomain.name: x-gw-subdomain
XGwSubdomain.description: Workfront customer subdomain (e.g. `mycompany`). Must match the subdomain of the Workfront instance being accessed. Passing an incorrect or unrecognized subdomain will result in a `502 Bad Gateway` response from the AIO gateway.

WfUserId.name: wf-userid
WfUserId.description: ID of the Workfront user the request acts as.

Approval.description: An approval record for an asset

realCreatorId.description: ID of the proxy user who actually created the approval. When the approval is created on behalf of another user (e.g. via a technical account or another proxying integration), this is the ID of the actual user making the call (the technical-account / proxy user). The companion `creatorId` field still reflects the user the action is attributed to. When no proxying takes place, this matches the companion field.

templateId.description: ID of the template used to create this approval, if any.

productId.description: Identifier of the Workfront product the approval is associated with. Always `workfront` for the Unified Approvals Connector.

status.description:
Overall lifecycle status of the approval, derived from the rolled-up stage and participant decisions.

- `in review` — At least one stage is active and waiting for decisions.
- `pending review` — Approval exists but no stage has been activated yet.
- `approved` — All required participants have approved.
- `approved with changes` — All required participants have decided; at least one with changes.
- `needs work` — At least one required participant has returned needs work.
- `reviewed` — All reviewer-role participants have reviewed (no approver decisions required).
- `withdrawn` — The approval has been retracted; no further actions are possible.

isLocked.description: Whether the approval is currently locked. Mirrors the lock state of the active stage (a stage being manually locked sets the approval inactive).

isLockOverridden.description: Whether the approval lock was overridden by an admin.

isApprovalActive.description: Computed flag that indicates whether the version being accessed is still the document's active (head) version. Compares the document's `currentVersionID` against the `assetId` of the requested version: when they match, the version is current and `isApprovalActive` is `true`; when the document has been superseded by a newer upload, it is `false`.

isEsmAsset.description: Whether the asset is an ESM (Experience Storage Manager) asset

frameSyncStatus.description: Whether the Frame.io asset sync is complete

stages.description: Ordered list of stages on this approval.

structure.description: Stage dependency graph. Each entry maps a `stageId` to its `parentIds`, defining the order in which stages activate.

paths.description: Parallel approval paths on this approval. Each path has its own `stages` and `structure`, allowing independent stage sequences to run side by side. Empty for single-path approvals.

userInfo.description: Contextual information about the authenticated user's relationship to this approval

isEditable.description: Whether the requesting user can make changes to this approval. Computed per request as `canEdit AND isActive AND hasLicenseAccess` — the user must have edit permission on the underlying asset, the approval must be in an active state, and the user must have a Workfront license tier that grants edit access. Used by write-path middleware to gate mutating requests and surfaced on every approval response so consumers can mirror the same gate in the UI.

hasLicenseAccess.description: Whether the requesting user's Workfront license tier grants the access needed to edit this approval. One of the inputs to `isEditable`.

activeDecision.description: The current user's most recent decision

action.description:
The next decision-related action the requesting user can take on this approval, derived from the user's `participantRole` and current `activeDecision`. Frontends typically render this as a button label.

| Role / Decision | `userInfo.action` |
|---|---|
| `approver` (no decision yet) | `approve` |
| `reviewer` (no decision yet) | `review` |
| Decision = `approved` | `revoke` |
| Decision = `needs work` | `approve` |
| Decision = `reviewed` | `review` |

availableDecisions.description: Map of decision key to display label for the current user

stageId.description: Identifier for this stage. Must be unique across all stages on the approval. Can be a short, human-readable slug (e.g. `design-review`).

pathId.description: ID of the path this stage belongs to, when the stage is part of a multi-path approval.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of the stage.

- `not started` — Stage has not yet been triggered to `isActive`. Set on creation and remains until the stage's activation trigger fires (typically when its parent stages complete).
- `pending review` — Stage is active and awaiting participant decisions.
- `in review` — Stage is active and at least one participant has not yet decided.
- `approved` — All required participants on this stage have approved.
- `approved with changes` — All required participants have decided, at least one has chosen `approved with changes`, and the rest have chosen `approved` or `approved with changes`. If any required participant has returned `needs work`, the stage rolls up to `needs work` instead.
- `needs work` — At least one required participant has responded with `needs work`. `needs work` outranks `approved` and `approved with changes`, so the stage rolls up to this status whenever any required participant has returned `needs work`.
- `reviewed` — All reviewer participants have reviewed.

deadlineTime.description: Deadline time of day in 24-hour `HH:MM` format (e.g. `"17:00"`).

deadlineTimeOfDay.description:
Time-of-day component of the stage deadline. An object with two numeric properties — `hours` (0–23) and `minutes` (0–59) — that, paired with the date derived from `deadlineBusinessDays`, pins the deadline to a specific moment. Set to `null` when no time-of-day is configured.

Example: `{ "hours": 17, "minutes": 0 }` for 5:00 PM.

isLocked.description: Stage has been manually locked (set inactive).

isLockOverridden.description: Stage lock was overridden by an admin.

isStarted.description: Stage has been started at least once.

isCompleted.description: Stage has reached a terminal state.

stageMetadata.description: Almost entirely a Frame.io integration artifact — when a Frame.io share is created for the stage it holds the generated review link and comments link. Defaults to `{}` if no Frame share was created (for example, on non-ESM or non-Frame assets).

parentIds.description: IDs of stages that must complete before this stage activates.

customMessage.description: Optional message sent to participants when this stage is activated

participantRole.description:
Role this participant plays on the stage.

- `approver` — Has a binding vote; their decision directly affects stage and approval status.
- `reviewer` — Non-binding; can mark reviewed but does not block approval progression.

The role, combined with the participant's current decision, also drives the `userInfo.action` value on every approval response — see [`Approval.userInfo.action`](#section/Schemas/Approval) for the role/decision → action mapping.

requesterId.description: ID of the user who added this participant

realRequesterId.description: ID of the proxy user who actually added this participant to the stage. When the participant is added on behalf of another user (e.g. via a technical account or another proxying integration), this is the ID of the actual user making the call (the technical-account / proxy user). The companion `requesterId` field still reflects the user the action is attributed to. When no proxying takes place, this matches the companion field.

status.description:
Lifecycle status of this participant on the stage.

- `notified` — Participant has been sent a notification but has not yet opened or decided.
- `opened` — Participant has opened the review but has not yet decided.
- `commented` — Participant has left a comment but has not made a final decision.
- `approved` — Participant has approved.
- `approved with changes` — Participant has approved with changes requested.
- `needs work` — Participant returned needs work.
- `reviewed` — Participant has marked the review complete (reviewer role only).
- `not started` — Participant is on a stage that has not yet become active; no notification has been sent.

realUserId.description: ID of the proxy user who actually performed the activity. When the activity is performed on behalf of another user (e.g. via a technical account or another proxying integration), this is the ID of the actual user making the call (the technical-account / proxy user). The companion `userId` field still reflects the user the action is attributed to. When no proxying takes place, this matches the companion field.

autoLockEnabled.description: Automatically lock the stage when all participants have decided

decisionRules.description: Override rule for when the stage is considered decided. `onlyOneDecisionRequired` marks the stage complete when any one participant decides.

StageTrigger.description: Defines when and how a stage is automatically activated

when.description: `onCreate` activates the stage immediately when the approval is created. `onStagesComplete` activates after specified parent stages complete.

stages.description: Stage IDs that must complete to fire this trigger (used with `onStagesComplete`)

allowedDecisions.description: Decisions that count as 'complete' for this trigger

ApprovalStructure.description: Represents one node in the stage dependency graph

stageId.description: Identifier of the stage this structure node represents. Matches the `stageId` on one of the approval's `stages[]` entries; must be unique across all stages on the approval (e.g. `design-review`).

parentIds.description: IDs of stages that must complete before this stage activates.

ApprovalPath.description: One parallel path on an approval that has multiple independent stage sequences. Each path carries its own `stages` and `structure`, scoped the same way as the top-level fields of the same name on `Approval`.

pathId.description: Identifier for this path. Must be unique across all paths on the approval.

status.description: Rollup status of this path, derived the same way as the approval-level `status` but scoped to this path's stages.

stages.description: Ordered list of stages on this path.

structure.description: Stage dependency graph for this path. Each entry maps a `stageId` to its `parentIds`, defining the order in which this path's stages activate.

StageBody.description: Stage definition used when creating or updating an approval

stageId.description: Optional client-assigned identifier for this stage, unique within the approval. If omitted, the server generates one. Use human-readable values (e.g. "legal-review") when referencing this stage in another stage's parentIds for sequential approval flows.

deadlineTime.description: Deadline time of day in 24-hour `HH:MM` format (e.g. `"17:00"`).

stageMetadata.description: Almost entirely a Frame.io integration artifact — when a Frame.io share is created for the stage it holds the generated review link and comments link. Defaults to `{}` if no Frame share was created (for example, on non-ESM or non-Frame assets).

participantRole.description:
Role this participant plays on the stage.

- `approver` — Has a binding vote; their decision directly affects stage and approval status.
- `reviewer` — Non-binding; can mark reviewed but does not block approval progression.

The role, combined with the participant's current decision, also drives the `userInfo.action` value on every approval response — see [`Approval.userInfo.action`](#section/Schemas/Approval) for the role/decision → action mapping.

parentIds.description: IDs of stages that must complete before this stage activates.

customMessage.description: Optional message for participants when this stage activates

pathId.description: ID of the path this stage belongs to, when the stage is part of a multi-path approval.

ApprovalPathCreate.description: One parallel path used when creating a multi-path approval.

pathId.description: Identifier for this path. Must be unique across all paths on the approval.

ApprovalPathUpdate.description: One parallel path used when replacing all stages on an existing multi-path approval.

pathId.description: Identifier for this path. Must be unique across all paths on the approval.

stages.description: Replacement stage definitions for this path.

ParticipantBody.description: Participant definition used in request bodies

stageId.description: ID of an existing stage on the approval to attach this participant to (e.g. `design-review`).

participantId.description: ID of the user or team to add. Required for every participant.

participantRole.description:
Role this participant plays on the stage.

- `approver` — Has a binding vote; their decision directly affects stage and approval status.
- `reviewer` — Non-binding; can mark reviewed but does not block approval progression.

The role, combined with the participant's current decision, also drives the `userInfo.action` value on every approval response — see [`Approval.userInfo.action`](#section/Schemas/Approval) for the role/decision → action mapping.

timeframeEstimate.description: Computed timeframe estimate, in business days, derived from the sum of each stage's `deadlineBusinessDays` value. Read-only.

structure.description: Workflow structure defining stage ordering and trigger dependencies.

paths.description: Parallel paths on this template. Each path has its own `stages` and `structure`, allowing independent stage sequences to run side by side. Empty for single-path templates.

timeframe.description: **Deprecated.** Use `timeframeEstimate` instead. Previously used to store the expected duration of the approval in days.

stageId.description: Identifier for this template stage. Must be unique across all stages within the template (e.g. `design-review`).

deadlineTimeOfDay.description:
Time-of-day component of the stage deadline. An object with two numeric properties — `hours` (0–23) and `minutes` (0–59) — that, paired with the date derived from `deadlineBusinessDays`, pins the deadline to a specific moment. Set to `null` when no time-of-day is configured.

Example: `{ "hours": 17, "minutes": 0 }` for 5:00 PM.

TemplatePath.description: One parallel path on a template that has multiple independent stage sequences. Each path carries its own `stages` and `structure`, scoped the same way as the top-level fields of the same name on `Template`.

pathId.description: Identifier for this path. Must be unique across all paths on the template.

structure.description: Stage dependency graph for this path. Each entry maps a `stageId` to its `parentIds`, defining the order in which this path's stages activate.

participantType.description:
Type of participant.

- `USER` — Individual Workfront user (or AI bot user).
- `TEAMOB` — Workfront team.

participantRole.description:
Role this participant plays on the stage.

- `approver` — Has a binding vote; their decision directly affects stage and approval status.
- `reviewer` — Non-binding; can mark reviewed but does not block approval progression.

The role, combined with the participant's current decision, also drives the `userInfo.action` value on every approval response — see [`Approval.userInfo.action`](#section/Schemas/Approval) for the role/decision → action mapping.

emailAddr.description: User's email address. Populated only when `participantType` is `USER`.

licenseType.description: Workfront license tier of the user. Populated only when `participantType` is `USER`.

eauthUserID.description: IMS-bound external authentication user ID. Populated only when `participantType` is `USER`.

avatarDate.description: Avatar version timestamp used to bust the avatar image cache. Populated only when `participantType` is `USER`.

TemplateBody.description: Request body for creating or updating a template.

assetType.description: Asset type the template applies to.

stages.description: Stages that make up the template, in graph form.

paths.description: Parallel paths that make up the template, each with its own stages in graph form. Omit for single-path templates.

sharedWith.description: Optional list of users the template is shared with.

TemplateStageBody.description: A single stage in graph form, used when creating or updating a template (either directly under `stages`, or nested under one of `paths[].stages`).

stageId.description: Identifier for this template stage. Must be unique across all stages within the template (e.g. `design-review`).

parentIds.description: IDs of stages that must complete before this stage activates.

triggers.description: Activation triggers for the stage. Each entry defines when and how the stage becomes active relative to other stages on the template.

deadlineBusinessDays.description: Number of business days from stage activation to its deadline.

deadlineTimeOfDay.description:
Time-of-day component of the stage deadline. An object with two numeric properties — `hours` (0–23) and `minutes` (0–59) — that, paired with the date derived from `deadlineBusinessDays`, pins the deadline to a specific moment. Set to `null` when no time-of-day is configured.

Example: `{ "hours": 17, "minutes": 0 }` for 5:00 PM.

participantType.description:
Type of participant.

- `USER` — Individual Workfront user (or AI bot user).
- `TEAMOB` — Workfront team.

participantRole.description:
Role this participant plays on the stage.

- `approver` — Has a binding vote; their decision directly affects stage and approval status.
- `reviewer` — Non-binding; can mark reviewed but does not block approval progression.

TemplatePathBody.description: One parallel path in graph form, used when creating or updating a multi-path template.

pathId.description: Identifier for this path. Must be unique across all paths on the template.

stages.description: Stages that make up this path, in graph form.

response.description: Upstream service error response, if applicable

source.description: Which upstream produced the error (for example `workfront` or `aas`). Only present on operations that call more than one upstream, where the HTTP status alone cannot tell you which one failed.

guidelineAttribute.description: Attribute of the guideline being evaluated.

isBot.description: Whether this user is an AI bot participant.

participantIdType.description:
How `participantId` is typed:
- `wf_guid` — non-ESM assets.
- `ims` — ESM assets with an IMS `eauthUserID`.
- `email` — ESM assets without an IMS `eauthUserID`.

wfUserId.description: The Workfront internal user ID (32-character hex).

emailAddr.description: User's email address. Omitted when not available from Workfront.

isBot.description: Whether this team is an AI bot participant.

ParticipantMetadata.description:
Free-form metadata about the participant. The shape varies by `participantType`:

**`USER` participants**
```
{
  "isBot": boolean,
  "participantIdType": "wf_guid" | "ims" | "email",
  "wfUserId": "string",
  "emailAddr": "string"  // omitted when not available
}
```

**`TEAMOB` (team) participants**
```
{
  "isBot": boolean
}
```

See `ParticipantUserMetadata` and `ParticipantTeamMetadata` for the typed shapes. Additional context-specific properties may be present; consumers should treat unknown keys as informational.

TeamMember.description: Workfront user that is a member of a team participant.

ParticipantUserWfMetadata.description: Workfront-derived enrichment fields populated when `participantType` is `USER`.

avatarDate.description: Avatar version timestamp used to bust avatar cache.

ParticipantTeamWfMetadata.description: Workfront-derived enrichment fields populated when `participantType` is `TEAMOB`.

ParticipantWfMetadata.description: Workfront-derived enrichment fields for the participant. The shape depends on `participantType` — see `ParticipantUserWfMetadata` and `ParticipantTeamWfMetadata`.

ApprovalDeletedResponse.description: Returned when removing the last remaining participant on the approval causes the approval itself to be deleted. The body contains user-context flags only (no approval payload), with `deleted: true` to signal the cascading delete.

deleted.description: Always `true` on this response shape; the approval no longer exists.

isApprovalActive.description: Whether the version being accessed is the document's active head version.

totalGuidelineTraitsPassed.description: Number of guideline traits that passed.

totalCriticalGuidelineTraitsPassed.description: Number of critical guideline traits that passed.

totalNonCriticalGuidelineTraitsPassed.description: Number of non-critical guideline traits that passed.

validationSummary.description: Aggregate result across all checks for the asset (or page).

passed.description: Whether the asset passed validation overall.

imageGuidelines.description: Aggregate guideline-trait counts plus an overall pass flag and score.

totalGuidelineTraitsPassed.description: Number of guideline traits that passed.

totalCriticalGuidelineTraitsPassed.description: Number of critical guideline traits that passed.

totalNonCriticalGuidelineTraitsPassed.description: Number of non-critical guideline traits that passed.

fieldResults.description: Per-field validation results, keyed by field name.

botId.description: ID of the bot that produced this review.

brandId.description: ID of the brand associated with the bot.

categoryId.description: Category for this review, if any.

validationTypes.description: Validation types applied to this asset.

stageId.description: ID of the approval stage this review is attached to.

pdfDownloadUrl.description: Pre-signed URL to download a PDF of the review, when available.

bot.description: Display name of the bot at the time of review.

status.description: Lifecycle status of the review (e.g. completed, failed).

failureCode.description: Machine-readable failure code when the review could not complete.

multiPageValidationResult.description: Per-page validation results for multi-page assets, keyed by page identifier. Each value follows the same shape as `validationResult`.

PartialApproval.description: Returned by GET approval when no approval exists for the asset yet. Contains only the contextual fields that can be computed without an approval record.

isApprovalActive.description: Whether the requested asset is the current version of the document. `false` when the asset is not the current version.

isEsmAsset.description: Whether the asset is stored in external storage (ESM).

frameSyncStatus.description: Whether the asset has finished syncing to Frame. `null` when there is no sync record for the asset.

isEditable.description: Whether the requesting user can create or modify an approval for this asset.

hasLicenseAccess.description: Whether the requesting user's license tier grants edit access.

EmptyApproval.description: Returned within the bulk lookup `approvals` array for asset IDs that have no approval. Contains only `assetId` and `frameSyncStatus`.

assetId.description: The asset ID that was queried.

frameSyncStatus.description: Whether the asset has finished syncing to Frame. `null` when there is no sync record for the asset.

TemplateDeleteResult.description: Result of a bulk template delete.

deleted.description: Template IDs that were successfully deleted.

failed.description: Template IDs that were not deleted (e.g. a permission denial or an AAS delete failure).

errors.description: Per-ID error details for IDs not deleted due to an upstream problem (e.g. an AuthZ failure) — distinct from a permission denial in `failed`.

role.description: Participant role on the stage (e.g. approver, reviewer).

participantMetadata.description: Optional free-form key/value metadata for this participant.

stageId.description: Client-assigned stage identifier, unique across all paths in the approval (not just within its own path).

parentIds.description: stageIds this stage depends on. Empty for a first stage; a stage activates once its parents complete.

participants.description: Approvers/reviewers on this stage. At most 50.

deadlineBusinessDays.description: Deadline expressed as a number of business days from activation.

customMessage.description: Optional message included in stage notifications.

GroupedApprovalPathInput.description: An approval path: an ordered set of stages that the group's assets move through.

pathId.description: Client-assigned path identifier (used on updates to match an existing path).

stages.description: The ordered stages of the path. At most 10.

name.description: Display name of the grouped approval.

parentId.description: Workfront parent object ID to associate with this grouped approval. Requires objCode.

objCode.description: Workfront parent object type code (e.g. PROJ, TASK). Required when parentId is set.

templateId.description: Optional ID of an existing approval template. It is recorded on the grouped approval and counted toward the template's usage; stages are **not** copied from the template, so `paths` is still required. An unknown ID returns `404`.

assets.description: Document version (DOCV) IDs to include in the group. At most 25.

paths.description: One or more approval paths, each a sequence of stages. At most 3. The number of assets multiplied by the total number of stages across all paths cannot exceed 100; a larger group returns `400 GROUP_ASSET_STAGE_CAP_EXCEEDED` (for example, 25 assets allows at most 4 stages in total).

GroupedApprovalUnifiedUpdate.description: The complete desired state of a grouped approval. The current state is compared with what you send and the difference is applied atomically (all or nothing). Paths and stages are matched by `pathId` and `stageId`: one that matches an existing item updates it, one that does not is created, and **any existing path or stage you leave out is removed**. `assets` is optional: send it to set the complete list of assets, or leave it out to keep the group's assets as they are. The order of `paths`, and of `stages` within a path, is the order the group ends up in. The group's size is also capped: the number of assets multiplied by the total number of stages across all paths cannot exceed 100, and a request that would grow the group past that returns `400 GROUP_ASSET_STAGE_CAP_EXCEEDED` (for example, 25 assets allows at most 4 stages in total).

name.description: Optional new name for the grouped approval. Omit it to keep the current name.

paths.description: The complete set of approval paths for the group.

assets.description: Optional. The complete set of document version (DOCV) IDs the group should contain; assets you leave out are removed. Omit the field to leave the group's assets unchanged. When you send `assets` it must list at least one ID; an empty list returns `400`.

idempotencyKey.description: Optional key identifying one logical save. When you retry the same request with the same key, new paths and stages that have no `pathId` or `stageId` are given the same generated IDs each time, so the retry does not create duplicates. It does not otherwise deduplicate requests; without it, retrying a request that creates paths or stages without IDs can create them twice.

GroupedApprovalUpdatePathInput.description: A path in a full-state update. A `pathId` that matches an existing path updates it; omitting `pathId`, or sending one that does not match, creates a new path. A new `pathId` that is already used by another path in the group (including a deleted one) returns `409 DUPLICATE_PATH_IN_GROUP`.

pathId.description: Path identifier. Matches an existing path, or names a new one.

stages.description: The complete, ordered set of stages for the path. Existing stages you leave out are removed.

GroupedApprovalUpdateStageInput.description:
A stage in a full-state update. A `stageId` that matches an existing stage on the same path updates it; omitting `stageId`, or sending one that does not match, creates a new stage. A new `stageId` must be unique across every path in the group, otherwise the request fails with `409 STAGE_ID_CONFLICT`. For a stage that already exists, `parentIds` is ignored.

On a **new** path, send `parentIds` on every stage (an empty array for the first stage) or on none. If you send `parentIds`, every stage must also have a `stageId` so the stages can refer to each other, and a stage cannot list itself as a parent; otherwise the request fails with `400`. Triggers are derived from `parentIds` and cannot be supplied.

stageId.description: Stage identifier. Matches an existing stage on this path, or names a new one.

put.description:

Team membership is looked up from the caller's Workfront session. A request authenticated with only a bearer token has no session, so it is matched only against participants listed individually, not against teams the user belongs to.

Replaces the complete desired state of a grouped approval (name, paths, stages, participants and assets) in one call. The current state is compared with the request and the difference is applied atomically: either every change is made or none are.

Paths and stages are matched by `pathId` and `stageId`. One that matches updates the existing item, one that does not is created, and any existing path or stage you leave out is removed. Assets are only reconciled when you send `assets`: the list you send is the complete set (assets you leave out are removed), and leaving `assets` out keeps the group's assets as they are. To change only part of a group, use the narrower operations instead: rename, assets, stages, stage participants or stage metadata.

A stage that is locked cannot be changed (`409`), and `assets`, when sent, must list at least one ID (an empty list returns `400`). Use `idempotencyKey` to make a retried save safe.

patch.summary: Manage stages on a grouped approval
patch.description: Adds, updates and/or removes stages on a grouped approval. Operations are processed in the order remove, then update, then add.

post.description:
Searches the approvals the requesting user can see, filtered by any combination of the fields below, and returns one page of results. Pass the `cursor` from a response back in the next request to get the following page; `cursor` is `null` when there are no more results.

`projectId` and `folderId` are resolved to the document versions in that project or folder, so a project with no documents returns an empty `data` array, and a project or folder that has no document matching your `assetType` or `assetId` returns `400`.

projectId.description: Only approvals on documents in this Workfront project (one ID or a list).

folderId.description: Only approvals on documents in this Workfront folder. Use `null` for the root folder of the project.

assetType.description: Only approvals on this asset type (for example `DOCV`).

assetId.description: Only approvals on these asset IDs.

creatorId.description: Only approvals created by this user.

createdDateFrom.description: Only approvals created at or after this time.

createdDateTo.description: Only approvals created at or before this time.

stageStatus.description: Only approvals that have a stage with this status.

stageDeadlineDateFrom.description: Only stages with a deadline at or after this time.

stageDeadlineDateTo.description: Only stages with a deadline at or before this time.

participantType.description: Only approvals with a participant of this type.

participantId.description: Only approvals this participant is on.

participantRole.description: Only approvals where a participant has this role.

participantStatus.description: Only approvals where a participant has this status.

overdue.description: When `true`, only approvals with a stage deadline in the past. If `stageDeadlineDateTo` is missing or in the future it is set to the current time.

view.description:
Shape of the result rows.

- `full` — the complete approval, with its stages and participants (default).
- `full_with_paths` — `full`, plus each parallel path's own stages and structure in `paths`.
- `personalApprovals` — only approvals the requesting user is a participant on.
- `participants` — one row per participant instead of per approval; rows have no `assetId`.

cursor.description: Cursor from the previous response, to get the next page. Omit for the first page.

data.description: Result rows, in the shape of the requested `view`.

cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or `null` if there are no more results.
